findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping in document lookups
findings.body: When a caller supplies another tenant’s document ID, `getDocument` still receives `ctx.tenantId`, but the changed call and query discard it and search only by `documentId`. Unless the database independently enforces tenant isolation, this can return another tenant’s document. Retain `tenantId` in the lookup predicate.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the existing `loadDocument` argument contract
findings.body:
Existing callers using `loadDocument(db, tenantId, documentId)` now either fail TypeScript compilation due to the changed arity or, in JavaScript, use `tenantId` as the document ID and return incorrect results.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore the exported cache module
findings.body:
Deleting `src/cache.ts` breaks existing consumers or tests importing `readCached`, producing a module-not-found compile/runtime error.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when loading documents
findings.body:
In a shared multi-tenant database, an authenticated caller can supply another tenant’s document ID and retrieve it because the query no longer constrains `tenantId`; `ctx.tenantId` is completely ignored, creating a cross-tenant authorization bypass and data disclosure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
